topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, welcome, and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional local and systemic cancer interventions—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic approaches that exploit specific inherent weaknesses in cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and managing drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the rationale and mechanisms of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting hyperactive oncogenic drivers, as well as the diverse resistance mechanisms and dosing strategies associated with them.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and therapeutic mechanisms of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor cell surface antigens.

topics.label: T-cell immunology and cancer immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the role of immune surveillance and the development of strategies to engage or engineer T cells against cancer, including checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Overall progress, future directions, and ethical dilemmas in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess broad challenges in modern oncology, historical mortality trends, emerging paradigms in management and detection, and the ethical dilemmas of clinical trials.
